epithet.en: A fat knight short of money in Windsor

1.modern-en: Falstaff is at Page's door, accused by Justice Shallow of poaching deer and breaking into the lodge, and brushes off the complaint.

3.modern-en: Falstaff dismisses Pistol and Nym from the Garter Inn for refusing to carry his love letters to Mistress Ford and Mistress Page.

6.modern-en: Falstaff receives Mistress Quickly's encouraging report at the Garter and then receives the disguised Master Ford as 'Brook,' who pays him to seduce his own wife.

10.modern-en: Falstaff comes to Mistress Ford's house and is hustled into a buck-basket full of foul linen and carried off to be dumped in the Thames.

12.modern-en: Falstaff drips back into the Garter Inn after the river, is consoled with sack, and is persuaded by Mistress Quickly to try Mistress Ford again.

13.modern-en: Falstaff is seen in the street still complaining about the dunking.

14.modern-en: Falstaff returns to Mistress Ford and is rushed by her into the disguise of the fat witch of Brentford, then beaten through the streets by Master Ford.

17.modern-en: Falstaff sits at the Garter telling Simple — and then Mistress Quickly — that he has been twice played upon.

19.modern-en: Falstaff agrees, after much persuading, to a third meeting with the wives in Windsor Park at Herne's Oak, wearing the antlers of the ghost-hunter.

23.modern-en: Falstaff arrives at Herne's Oak at midnight in stag horns, is set upon by Windsor children dressed as fairies, and pinched and burned until he gives in.

epithet.en: Wife to Master Ford, one of the merry wives

5.modern-en: Mistress Ford compares her love letter from Falstaff with Mistress Page's identical one and plans the revenge.

10.modern-en: Mistress Ford receives Falstaff at her house, gets him into the buck-basket of dirty linen, and has the servants carry it out as her husband returns.

14.modern-en: Mistress Ford disguises Falstaff as the fat woman of Brentford and lets her husband beat 'her' through the streets.

16.modern-en: Mistress Ford, with her husband finally in the joke, helps plan the final fairy trick at Herne's Oak.

21.modern-en: Mistress Ford goes over the costuming for the children's masque in Windsor Park.

23.modern-en: Mistress Ford and Mistress Page entice Falstaff to Herne's Oak under the antlers and stage the fairy ambush.

epithet.en: Wife to Master Page, the other merry wife

5.modern-en: Mistress Page reads her love letter from Falstaff aloud to herself, then to Mistress Ford, and helps plot the revenge.

11.modern-en: Mistress Page sits at home with Anne and Fenton and tells him quietly that she favours Doctor Caius's suit, not his.

16.modern-en: Mistress Page invents the Herne's Oak fairy plan and arranges the children's costumes.

21.modern-en: Mistress Page slips word to her favoured suitor Caius to carry off the green-clad Anne at the fairy masque.

23.modern-en: Mistress Page co-leads the children's ambush of Falstaff at the oak.

epithet.en: The jealous husband, also disguised as 'Master Brook'

6.modern-en: Master Ford, in his Brook disguise, hires Falstaff to seduce his own wife so he can catch her in the act.

9.modern-en: Master Ford eavesdrops on Page and others in the street and decides to spring on Falstaff at the appointed hour.

10.modern-en: Master Ford comes home with friends to catch Falstaff and finds nothing but a buck-basket of linen on its way to the laundress.

14.modern-en: Master Ford comes home a second time, beats the disguised Falstaff as the witch of Brentford, and is left more bewildered than vindicated.

16.modern-en: Master Ford is finally let in on his wife's joke and joins the planning of the Herne's Oak ambush.

epithet.en: Anne's father, husband of Mistress Page

1.modern-en: Master Page welcomes Shallow, Slender, and the Falstaff company at his door and invites them in to dinner.

5.modern-en: Master Page laughs off any thought that Falstaff would seduce his wife, and quietly favours Slender as a son-in-law.

7.modern-en: Master Page is in the field with Caius and the others where a duel has been arranged.

9.modern-en: Master Page advises Ford against his suspicions in the street.

16.modern-en: Master Page joins the final fairy plan and quietly arranges with Slender to carry off the white-clad Anne.

19.modern-en: Master Page is at the Garter Inn during the planning.

23.modern-en: Master Page is at the masque at Herne's Oak in his role as a parent and helper.

epithet.en: The Pages' young daughter, courted by three suitors

1.modern-en: Anne brings out wine to the guests and is unenthusiastically introduced to Slender.

11.modern-en: Anne meets Fenton in her father's house and tells him she loves him over her parents' preferred candidates.

16.modern-en: Anne is given her role in the children's fairy masque.

21.modern-en: Anne is dressed for the masque in green to escape with Fenton while her parents have arranged white or red for their two preferred suitors.

epithet.en: A young gentleman, Anne Page's true love

11.modern-en: Fenton calls on Anne at the Page house and is rebuffed at the door by her father, who suspects him of fortune-hunting.

18.modern-en: Fenton confides in the Host of the Garter and arranges the secret marriage during the fairy masque.

epithet.en: Justice Shallow's nephew, a foolish suitor of Anne

1.modern-en: Slender is brought to Page's house by his uncle Shallow and is introduced as a possible match for Anne.

11.modern-en: Slender is mentioned as Master Page's preferred suitor for Anne.

16.modern-en: Slender is told by Page to look for the white-clad bride at the masque.

epithet.en: A French physician living in Windsor, suitor of Anne

4.modern-en: Doctor Caius discovers Sir Hugh's servant Simple hidden in his closet, learns of the Welsh parson's matchmaking, and challenges him to a duel.

7.modern-en: Doctor Caius waits in a field outside Windsor for Sir Hugh to arrive for the duel.

8.modern-en: Doctor Caius is led around the wrong field at Frogmore by the Host while Sir Hugh waits at another spot.

13.modern-en: Doctor Caius and Sir Hugh, finally reconciled, plot revenge on the Host of the Garter for the trick.

16.modern-en: Doctor Caius is told by Mistress Page to look for the green-clad bride at Herne's Oak.

1.modern-en: Sir Hugh tries to mediate the quarrel between Falstaff and Shallow and to broker the Anne-Slender match.

2.modern-en: Sir Hugh sends Simple with a letter to Mistress Quickly asking her to put in a good word for Slender.

7.modern-en: Sir Hugh waits in the field for Doctor Caius to arrive for their duel.

8.modern-en: Sir Hugh meets Caius in the wrong field, both having been led there by the Host.

13.modern-en: Sir Hugh and Caius, reconciled, plot to revenge themselves on the Host.

22.modern-en: Sir Hugh leads the Windsor children into the park dressed as fairies for the night's masque.

23.modern-en: Sir Hugh, dressed as a satyr, leads the children's pinches and burns on Falstaff at the oak.

epithet.en: Doctor Caius's housekeeper and Windsor's go-between

4.modern-en: Mistress Quickly tries to hide Simple in Doctor Caius's closet and then promises three different men to advance their suit with Anne.

6.modern-en: Mistress Quickly goes to Falstaff at the Garter Inn with the wives' invitations and reads Mistress Ford's heart to him.

12.modern-en: Mistress Quickly returns to the Garter Inn after the river dunking to persuade Falstaff to try once more.

17.modern-en: Mistress Quickly arrives at the Garter Inn with a new appointment from Mistress Ford.

23.modern-en: Mistress Quickly leads the fairy queen in the children's masque at Herne's Oak.

epithet.en: The keeper of the Garter Inn

3.modern-en: The Host welcomes Falstaff to the Garter Inn and lets Bardolph take service as a tapster.

7.modern-en: The Host promises to take both duellists to their separate fields and tease the situation along.

8.modern-en: The Host plays the trick on Caius and Sir Hugh, taking each to the wrong meeting-place.

15.modern-en: The Host is robbed of three of his horses by men passing themselves off as German visitors.

18.modern-en: The Host agrees to help Fenton elope with Anne and lend his cover at the masque.

19.modern-en: The Host is at the Garter as Falstaff prepares for the third assignation.
